title: Peel officers cleared in Ontario Taser death
article: Four Peel Regional police officers did not commit any criminal offences in the death of a man who died after being jolted with a Taser stun gun, Ontario's Special Investigations Unit said Wednesday.
Sean Reilly, 42, of Brampton, Ont., was arrested on Sept. 16 2008 at a home in Mississauga on a charge of assault with a weapon and taken to a cell at a police station on Dixie Road.

About 30 minutes later, Reilly was seen on a cell monitor banging his head on the bars, causing his forehead to bleed, according to the SIU, the provincial agency that investigates cases of serious injury or death involving police.
Officers got him to stop banging his head and entered the cell to subdue him, the SIU said.
Reilly ran at one of the officers who entered the jail cell, was shocked by a Taser and immediately fell into physical distress. He stopped breathing moments later, the SIU said.
Reilly was resuscitated by paramedics and taken to Mississauga General Hospital but he never regained consciousness. He was pronounced dead the next day.

A mandatory inquest will determine the cause of death, SIU director Ian Scott said Wednesday, but the forensic evidence indicates the force used by the officers against Reilly, including the Taser discharge, did not contribute to his death.

"Given the circumstances leading to the death of Mr. Reilly, I am of the view that the four subject officers' conduct fell within the limits prescribed by the criminal law," Scott said in a statement. "Accordingly, I cannot attach criminal liability to their acts and omissions with respect to this incident."
